notes: Original practice questions written to the official ESAT format (27 MCQs, 40 minutes per module, no calculator, no negative marking). Not official UAT-UK material.

questions.stem:
A shop raises the price of a jacket by 25%. In a sale it then reduces the new price by 20%. VAT of 20% is then added to the sale price, giving a final price of £96.

What was the original price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: Overall multiplier = 1.25 × 0.8 × 1.2 = 1.2, so original = 96 ÷ 1.2 = £80. The 25% rise and 20% cut cancel exactly (1.25 × 0.8 = 1).

questions.stem: Which of the following is equal to (3 + √5) / (3 − √5) ?
Given that v = √(2k/r − c), which of the following expresses r in terms of v, k and c?
questions.explanation: Square: v² = 2k/r − c, so v² + c = 2k/r, giving r = 2k/(v² + c).

questions.stem:
Two positive integers, both greater than 12, have a highest common factor of 12 and a lowest common multiple of 360.

How many different pairs of such integers are there? (The pair a, b is the same as the pair b, a.)
questions.explanation: Write the numbers as 12m and 12n with m, n coprime. Then LCM = 12mn = 360, so mn = 30. Coprime factor pairs of 30 are (1,30), (2,15), (3,10), (5,6). Both numbers exceed 12, so m, n > 1, leaving 3 pairs: (24,180), (36,120), (60,72).

questions.stem: What is the value of (6 × 10⁻³)² ÷ (1.2 × 10⁻⁴) ?

y is inversely proportional to the square of x.

x is increased by 25%. What is the percentage change in y?
questions.explanation: y ∝ 1/x², so the new y is 1/1.25² = 1/1.5625 = 0.64 of the old y: a 36% decrease. (0.64 itself is the multiplier, not the change.)

questions.stem:
The curve y = 2x² − 12x + 23 has a minimum point at (p, q).

What is the value of p + q ?
Two kiosks each charge a flat fee plus a cost per postcard. Kiosk P charges £2 plus 30p per card. Kiosk Q charges 50p plus 55p per card. At how many cards do the kiosks charge the same total?
questions.explanation: In pence, equality requires 200 + 30n = 50 + 55n. So 25n = 150 and n = 6.

questions.stem:
A, B, C and D lie in that order on a circle.

Angle ABC = 3x°, angle ADC = (2x + 30)° and angle BAD = (x + 50)°.

What is the size of angle BCD?
questions.explanation: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, so opposite angles sum to 180°: 3x + 2x + 30 = 180 → x = 30. Then BAD = 80°, so BCD = 180° − 80° = 100°.

questions.stem:
In triangle PQR, angle PQR = 90°, angle QPR = 30° and PR = 8 cm.

S is the point on PQ such that angle SRQ = 45°.

What is the length of PS?
questions.explanation: QR = 8 sin 30° = 4 and PQ = 8 cos 30° = 4√3. Triangle SQR is right-angled with a 45° angle at R, so SQ = QR = 4. PS = 4√3 − 4 = 4(√3 − 1).

questions.stem:
A solid is made from a cone fixed on top of a hemisphere. The flat face of the hemisphere and the base of the cone coincide and each has radius 3 cm. The total height of the solid is 7 cm.

What is the volume of the solid?

(Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³; volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h)
questions.explanation: Hemisphere: (2/3)π × 27 = 18π. The hemisphere takes 3 cm of the height, so the cone has height 4: (1/3)π × 9 × 4 = 12π. Total 30π cm³.

questions.stem:
Two bottles are mathematically similar. Their surface areas are in the ratio 9 : 16.

The larger bottle has a volume of 640 cm³. What is the volume of the smaller bottle?
questions.explanation: Area ratio 9 : 16 means length ratio 3 : 4 and volume ratio 27 : 64. Smaller volume = 640 × 27/64 = 270 cm³. (360 uses the area ratio; 480 uses the length ratio.)

questions.stem:
The mean of ten numbers is 14. Two of the numbers are removed and the mean of the remaining eight numbers is 12.5.

What is the mean of the two numbers that were removed?
questions.explanation: Total of ten = 140. Total of eight = 8 × 12.5 = 100. The two removed total 40, so their mean is 20.

questions.stem:
A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.

Given that at least one of the counters is red, what is the probability that both are red?
questions.explanation: P(both red) = 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56. P(at least one red) = 1 − P(both blue) = 1 − (3/8 × 2/7) = 50/56. Conditional probability = 20/50 = 2/5.

questions.stem:
A histogram shows the masses, m grams, of some apples.

The class 10 < m ≤ 25 has a frequency density of 4 per gram.
The class 25 < m ≤ 30 has a frequency density of 9 per gram.

Assuming the apples are evenly spread within each class, estimate the number of apples with masses between 20 g and 28 g.
questions.explanation: Frequencies: 4 × 15 = 60 and 9 × 5 = 45. From 20 to 25 is 5/15 of the first class: 20 apples. From 25 to 28 is 3/5 of the second: 27 apples. Total 47.

questions.stem:
A car loses 20% of its value at the end of every year.

After how many complete years is the car first worth less than one third of its original value?
questions.explanation: 0.8⁴ = 0.4096 (still more than 1/3); 0.8⁵ = 0.32768 (less than 1/3). So after 5 years. Note it is not 20% of the original each year: the loss compounds.

questions.stem:
The length of a rectangle is 12 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre. Its width is 5.0 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.

What is the upper bound of the area of the rectangle?
questions.explanation: Upper bounds: length 12.5 cm, width 5.05 cm. Upper bound of area = 12.5 × 5.05 = 63.125 cm².

questions.stem:
The first five terms of a sequence are 3, 8, 15, 24, 35.

What is the 20th term?
questions.explanation: Second differences are constant (2), so the nth term is n² + bn + c. Fitting gives n² + 2n. The 20th term is 400 + 40 = 440. (It is also (n + 1)² − 1.)

questions.stem:
Simplify fully:

(x² − 9)/(x² + x − 6) ÷ (x − 3)/(x − 2)
questions.explanation: (x − 3)(x + 3)/[(x + 3)(x − 2)] × (x − 2)/(x − 3) = 1. Every factor cancels.

questions.stem:
OA = a and OB = b (as vectors). M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on OM such that OP : PM = 2 : 1.

Which of the following is the vector AP?

Water flows through a pipe at a rate of 0.6 litres per second.

What is this rate in cubic metres per hour?
questions.explanation: 1 litre = 0.001 m³, so 0.6 L/s = 0.0006 m³/s. Multiply by 3600 s/h: 2.16 m³/h.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to the recurring decimal 0.2454545… (where the digits 45 repeat)?

A four-digit code uses only the digits 1 to 9, and no digit may be used more than once.

How many such codes are even numbers greater than 5000?
questions.explanation: First digit is 5–9 and last digit is 2, 4, 6 or 8. If the first digit is even (6 or 8): 2 × 3 choices for the last digit × 7 × 6 = 252. If the first digit is odd (5, 7, 9): 3 × 4 × 7 × 6 = 504. Total 756.

questions.stem: How many integers n satisfy both 3n − 7 < 2n + 4 and 2n + 4 ≤ 5n + 13 ?
questions.explanation: 3n − 7 < 2n + 4 gives n < 11. 2n + 4 ≤ 5n + 13 gives −9 ≤ 3n, so n ≥ −3. Integers −3, −2, …, 10: that is 14 integers.

questions.stem:
A train accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 40 s. It then travels at 20 m/s for T seconds, and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 30 s. The total distance travelled is 4.3 km.

What is the value of T?
questions.explanation: Distance = area under the speed–time graph = ½ × 40 × 20 + 20T + ½ × 30 × 20 = 400 + 20T + 300 = 4300. So 20T = 3600 and T = 180.

questions.stem:
A sector of a circle has radius 6 cm and angle 120°. Its two straight edges are joined, without overlap, to form the curved surface of a cone.

What is the perpendicular height of the cone?
questions.explanation: Arc length = (120/360) × 2π × 6 = 4π, which becomes the base circumference, so the base radius is 2. The slant height is 6, so height = √(36 − 4) = √32 = 4√2 cm.

questions.stem: Given that 4^(x + 1) × 8^x = 32^(2 − x), what is the value of x?
Which structures are found in a typical bacterial cell?

options.label: A
options.text: cell membrane, mitochondria, nucleus and plasmids

options.label: B
options.text: cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus and chloroplasts

options.label: C
options.text: cell membrane, cell wall, plasmid DNA and chromosomal DNA free in the cytoplasm

options.label: D
options.text: cell wall made of cellulose, mitochondria and a nucleus

options.label: E
options.text: cell membrane, chloroplasts, plasmids and a nucleus

options.label: F
options.text: cell wall, vacuole, nucleus and plasmids

questions.explanation: Prokaryotes have no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria or chloroplasts. Their DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm, often with plasmids.

questions.stem:
A strip of potato tissue is placed in a concentrated sugar solution for an hour.

Which describes what happens?

options.label: A
options.text: Water leaves the cells by osmosis, from a lower to a higher water potential, so the strip loses mass.

options.label: B
options.text: Sugar enters the cells by osmosis, so the strip gains mass.

options.label: C
options.text: Water leaves the potato cells by osmosis, from a higher to a lower water potential, so the strip loses mass.

options.label: D
options.text: Water leaves the cells by active transport, so the strip loses mass.

options.label: E
options.text: There is no change because potato cells have cell walls.

options.label: F
options.text: Water enters the potato cells by osmosis, from a higher to a lower water potential, so the strip gains mass.

questions.explanation: The concentrated solution has a lower water potential than the cell contents, so water moves out by osmosis (higher → lower water potential) and the strip loses mass. Osmosis refers to water, not solute.

questions.stem:
A cell in the testis of a mammal has 2n = 46 chromosomes and undergoes meiosis.

How many cells are produced, and how many chromosomes does each contain?
questions.explanation: Meiosis has two divisions, producing four genetically different haploid cells, each with one copy of each chromosome (23 in humans).

questions.stem: Which statement about cancer is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It occurs only in cells that cannot divide.

options.label: B
options.text: It results from changes in cells, including mutations, that lead to uncontrolled cell division.

options.label: C
options.text: It results from cells dividing by meiosis instead of mitosis.

options.label: D
options.text: It is caused only by bacteria.

options.label: E
options.text: It is caused by cells stopping DNA replication.

options.label: F
options.text: It is always inherited from a parent.

questions.explanation: Cancer is uncontrolled mitotic division after mutations affect the genes controlling the cell cycle.

questions.stem:
In a mammal, a male (XY) and a female (XX) have offspring.

What is the probability that their first two offspring are both female?
questions.explanation: Each offspring has a 1/2 chance of being female, independently. Two in a row: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.stem:
In pea plants, the allele for tall stems (T) is dominant to the allele for short stems (t). A heterozygous tall plant is crossed with a short plant, giving 240 offspring.

How many of the offspring would be expected to be tall?
questions.explanation: Tt × tt gives Tt : tt in the ratio 1 : 1, so half the offspring are tall: 120.

questions.stem:
In a family, two unaffected parents have an affected daughter and an unaffected son. The condition is controlled by a single gene on an autosome.

What is the probability that the unaffected son is a carrier (heterozygous)?
questions.explanation: The affected daughter of unaffected parents shows the condition is recessive and both parents are Aa. Their children are AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1. An unaffected child is AA or Aa, so P(Aa) = 2/3.

questions.stem: A student sorts the genotypes I (AA), II (Aa) and III (aa) by whether they are homozygous. Which row correctly lists the two genotypes the student should group together and why?

options.label: A
options.text: I and III: both are homozygous.

options.label: B
options.text: I and II: both have one copy of A.

options.label: C
options.text: II and III: both have zero copies of A.

options.label: D
options.text: I and II: both are homozygous.

options.label: E
options.text: II and III: both are homozygous.

options.label: F
options.text: I and III: both have two copies of A.

questions.explanation: In AA and aa, the two alleles within each genotype are identical. Aa has two different alleles and is heterozygous.

questions.stem:
In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 18% of the bases are adenine.

What percentage of the bases are guanine?
questions.explanation: A pairs with T, so T = 18% and A + T = 36%. G + C = 64%, and G = C, so G = 32%.

questions.stem:
A gene contains 1500 bases in the part that codes for a polypeptide (on one strand), including a stop triplet at the end.

How many amino acids are in the polypeptide?
questions.explanation: Bases are read as triplets: 1500/3 = 500 triplets. The final stop triplet codes for no amino acid, so 499 amino acids.

questions.stem: Which statement about gene mutations is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype.

options.label: D
options.text: Every mutation determines a new phenotype.

options.label: F
options.text: Mutations change the sequence of amino acids but never the DNA.

questions.explanation: A mutation changes the DNA base sequence. Most have no effect on the phenotype, some have a small effect, and occasionally one determines the phenotype.

questions.stem: In genetic engineering, which enzymes are used to cut DNA at specific sequences and to join DNA fragments?

options.label: C
options.text: cut: DNA ligase; join: DNA ligase

questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences; DNA ligase joins the inserted gene into the vector DNA.

questions.stem: Which statement about stem cells is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Embryonic stem cells can form only one type of cell.

options.label: C
options.text: Adult stem cells are multipotent and can form a limited range of cell types.

options.label: D
options.text: Stem cells cannot divide by mitosis.

options.label: E
options.text: Multipotent cells can differentiate into any cell type.

options.label: F
options.text: Adult stem cells are totipotent and can form a whole organism.

questions.explanation: Early embryonic cells can be totipotent; most embryonic stem cells are pluripotent (any cell type); adult stem cells are multipotent (a limited range).

questions.stem:
A population of bacteria is exposed to an antibiotic, and over many generations most of the bacteria become resistant.

Which explanation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The antibiotic killed only the resistant bacteria.

options.label: B
options.text: The bacteria learned to break down the antibiotic.

options.label: C
options.text: The antibiotic caused the bacteria to mutate in order to become resistant.

options.label: D
options.text: Each bacterium became resistant during its own lifetime and passed this on.

options.label: E
options.text: Some bacteria already carried a resistance mutation; they survived, reproduced and passed on the allele.

options.label: F
options.text: Resistant bacteria were produced by selective breeding.

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on existing variation. The mutation arose randomly; the antibiotic only selects for it, increasing the allele's frequency over generations.

questions.stem:
An enzyme from the human stomach is incubated with protein at different pH values at 37 °C.

At which pH is the rate of protein digestion likely to be highest?

options.label: F
options.text: The rate is the same at all pH values.

questions.explanation: Stomach protease (pepsin) works best in acid conditions around pH 2. Away from its optimum, the active site changes shape and fits the substrate less well.

questions.stem:
An enzyme is heated to 80 °C and then cooled to 37 °C. It no longer catalyses its reaction.

What is the best explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: Low temperature has stopped the enzyme working.

options.label: B
options.text: The enzyme has changed into a different substance with a new active site.

options.label: C
options.text: The enzyme has been used up in the reaction.

options.label: D
options.text: The shape of the active site has changed permanently, so the substrate no longer fits.

options.label: E
options.text: The enzyme molecules are moving too fast to bind.

questions.explanation: High temperature breaks bonds holding the protein's 3D shape. The enzyme is denatured and the change is not reversed on cooling.

questions.stem: What is the word equation for anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
questions.explanation: Animal cells convert glucose to lactic acid without oxygen. Yeast and plants produce ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: In a reflex arc, which is the correct sequence?

options.label: A
options.text: receptor → sensory neurone → brain → motor neurone → receptor

options.label: B
options.text: effector → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → receptor

options.label: C
options.text: receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector

options.label: D
options.text: receptor → relay neurone → sensory neurone → motor neurone → effector

options.label: E
options.text: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector

options.label: F
options.text: receptor → sensory neurone → motor neurone → relay neurone → effector

questions.explanation: Impulses pass from the receptor along the sensory neurone to a relay neurone in the CNS (often the spinal cord), then along the motor neurone to the effector.

questions.stem: Which statement about blood vessels is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Arteries carry blood towards the heart.

options.label: B
options.text: Veins carry blood at higher pressure than arteries.

options.label: D
options.text: Capillaries have thick walls to prevent leakage.

options.label: F
options.text: Arteries have thick, elastic walls to withstand high pressure.

questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood. Veins have valves and low pressure; capillary walls are one cell thick.

questions.stem: During inhalation, which changes take place in the thorax?

options.label: A
options.text: The diaphragm relaxes and domes upwards, thorax volume increases and pressure falls.

options.label: B
options.text: The intercostal muscles relax, thorax volume increases and pressure rises.

options.label: C
options.text: Air is pushed into the lungs because pressure in the thorax rises.

options.label: D
options.text: The diaphragm contracts, thorax volume decreases and pressure rises.

options.label: E
options.text: The diaphragm contracts, thorax volume increases and pressure rises.

options.label: F
options.text: The diaphragm contracts and flattens, the external intercostal muscles contract, thorax volume increases and pressure falls.

questions.explanation: Contracting the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thorax volume, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air flows in.

questions.stem: After a meal high in carbohydrate, which response occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: The pancreas secretes insulin, and the liver converts glucose to glycogen.

options.label: B
options.text: The pancreas secretes insulin, and the liver converts glycogen to glucose.

options.label: C
options.text: The pancreas secretes glucagon, and the liver converts glycogen to glucose.

options.label: D
options.text: The liver secretes insulin, and the pancreas stores glycogen.

options.label: F
options.text: The kidneys secrete glucagon to lower blood glucose.

questions.explanation: Raised blood glucose → pancreas releases insulin → cells take up glucose and the liver and muscles store it as glycogen: negative feedback.

questions.stem: A person is dehydrated after exercise. Which response occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: Less ADH is released, and a larger volume of dilute urine is produced.

options.label: B
options.text: The kidneys stop filtering the blood.

options.label: C
options.text: Less ADH is released, and the collecting ducts reabsorb more water.

options.label: D
options.text: More ADH is released, and a larger volume of dilute urine is produced.

options.label: E
options.text: More insulin is released to reduce water loss.

options.label: F
options.text: More ADH is released, the collecting ducts reabsorb more water, and a smaller volume of more concentrated urine is produced.

questions.explanation: ADH increases the permeability of the collecting ducts to water, so more water is reabsorbed and the urine is concentrated.

questions.stem: Which hormone, released by the pituitary gland, triggers ovulation?
questions.explanation: A surge of luteinising hormone (LH) triggers release of an egg. FSH stimulates follicle development; oestrogen and progesterone come from the ovaries.

questions.stem: How does a vaccine provide protection against a disease?

options.label: A
options.text: It contains white blood cells that destroy the pathogen.

options.label: B
options.text: It contains dead or inactive pathogens that stimulate lymphocytes to make antibodies and memory cells.

options.label: C
options.text: It stops the pathogen from mutating.

options.label: D
options.text: It contains antibodies made by another person.

options.label: E
options.text: It contains antibiotics that kill the pathogen.

options.label: F
options.text: It kills viruses directly inside body cells.

questions.explanation: Antigens on the dead or inactive pathogen trigger an immune response. Memory cells give a faster, larger secondary response on later infection.

questions.stem:
To estimate a population of snails, 40 snails are caught, marked and released. A week later, 50 snails are caught, of which 8 are marked.

What is the estimated population?
questions.explanation: Proportion marked in the second sample = 8/50, so the population N ≈ 40 × 50 / 8 = 250.

questions.stem:
On a sunny day with plenty of light, the rate of photosynthesis of a crop in a greenhouse stops increasing as light intensity rises further.

Which change would most likely increase the rate?

options.label: B
options.text: adding more nitrogen to the air

questions.explanation: At high light intensity, light is no longer limiting; another factor (usually CO₂ concentration, or temperature) is. Raising CO₂ increases the rate.

questions.stem:
A potometer shows that a leafy shoot takes up 1.8 cm³ of water in 15 minutes.

What is the rate of water uptake?
questions.explanation: Rate = volume ÷ time = 1.8 ÷ 15 = 0.12 cm³ per minute.

questions.stem: Iron has atomic number 26. How many protons, neutrons and electrons are there in one ⁵⁶Fe³⁺ ion?
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 26. Neutrons = 56 − 26 = 30. A 3+ ion has lost 3 electrons: 26 − 3 = 23.

questions.stem:
A sample of copper contains 69% ⁶³Cu and 31% ⁶⁵Cu by number of atoms.

What is the relative atomic mass of copper in this sample, to 1 decimal place?
Sulfur has atomic number 16. What is the electron configuration of the sulfide ion, S²⁻?
questions.explanation: A sulfur atom is 2,8,6. Gaining two electrons gives 2,8,8, the configuration of argon.

questions.stem:
A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its relative formula mass is 180.

What is its molecular formula?

(Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Moles in 100 g: C 40/12 = 3.33, H 6.7/1 = 6.7, O 53.3/16 = 3.33. Ratio 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH₂O (Mr 30). 180/30 = 6, so C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.stem:
Aluminium reacts with chlorine: 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃

5.4 g of aluminium is heated with 14.2 g of chlorine. What is the maximum mass of aluminium chloride that can form?

(Ar: Al = 27, Cl = 35.5)
questions.explanation: Al: 5.4/27 = 0.20 mol. Cl₂: 14.2/71 = 0.20 mol. 0.20 mol Al needs 0.30 mol Cl₂, so chlorine is limiting. AlCl₃ = 0.20 × 2/3 = 0.133 mol × 133.5 = 17.8 g. (19.6 g is just the total mass of reactants; 26.7 g assumes Al is limiting.)

questions.stem:
10.0 g of calcium carbonate reacts completely with excess hydrochloric acid:
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂

What volume of carbon dioxide is produced at room temperature and pressure?

(Ar: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; 1 mol of gas occupies 24 dm³ at rtp)
questions.explanation: Mr of CaCO₃ = 100, so 0.10 mol, giving 0.10 mol CO₂ = 0.10 × 24 = 2.4 dm³.

questions.stem:
25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid.

What is the concentration of the sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles acid = 0.0200 × 0.100 = 0.00200, so NaOH = 0.00400 mol in 0.0250 dm³: 0.160 mol/dm³. (0.080 forgets the 1 : 2 ratio.)

questions.stem:
Copper(II) oxide is reduced by hydrogen: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O

8.0 g of copper(II) oxide produces 5.08 g of copper. What is the percentage yield?

(Ar: O = 16, Cu = 63.5)
questions.explanation: Mr CuO = 79.5 ≈ 80, so about 0.10 mol CuO, which can give 0.10 mol Cu = 6.35 g. Yield = 5.08/6.35 × 100 = 80%.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of chromium in potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇?
questions.explanation: K is +1 (total +2), O is −2 (total −14). The two Cr atoms total +12, so each is +6.

questions.stem: Which reaction is an example of disproportionation?
questions.explanation: In disproportionation one element is both oxidised and reduced. Chlorine goes from 0 in Cl₂ to −1 in NaCl and +1 in NaClO.

questions.stem:
Zinc is added to copper(II) sulfate solution: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu

Which species is the oxidising agent?

options.label: D
options.text: There is no oxidising agent, as this is not a redox reaction.

questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidising agent: it oxidises Zn to Zn²⁺.

questions.stem:
Substance Z has a high melting point. It does not conduct electricity when solid but does conduct when molten or dissolved in water.

What type of structure does Z have?
questions.explanation: Ionic lattices have high melting points; the ions are fixed in the solid but free to move when molten or in solution, so only then does it conduct.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in one formula unit of aluminium sulfate?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ and SO₄²⁻ combine as Al₂(SO₄)₃: 2 Al + 3 S + 12 O = 17 atoms.

questions.stem: Which mixture of aqueous solutions would react?
questions.explanation: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide. Reactivity falls down Group 17 (F > Cl > Br > I), so Cl₂ displaces Br⁻: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂.

questions.stem:
In a paper chromatogram, a spot has moved 3.0 cm from the baseline and the solvent front has moved 7.5 cm from the baseline.

What is the Rf value of the spot?
questions.explanation: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 3.0/7.5 = 0.40. Rf is always less than 1.

questions.stem:
An acid solution has pH 2. It is diluted with water so that its volume becomes 1000 times larger.

What is the pH of the diluted solution?
questions.explanation: The H⁺ concentration falls by a factor of 1000 = 10³, and each factor of 10 raises the pH by 1. pH = 2 + 3 = 5. Diluting an acid can never make it alkaline.

questions.stem:
Phosphoric acid, H₃PO₄, is a triprotic acid.

What volume of 0.20 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide is needed to neutralise 0.010 mol of phosphoric acid completely?
questions.explanation: Each H₃PO₄ releases 3 H⁺, so 0.030 mol NaOH is needed. Volume = 0.030 ÷ 0.20 = 0.15 dm³ = 150 cm³.

questions.stem:
Magnesium ribbon reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid.

Which change would NOT increase the initial rate of reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: cutting the ribbon into small pieces

options.label: E
options.text: using magnesium powder instead of ribbon

options.label: F
options.text: using the same mass of magnesium as a single thicker piece

questions.explanation: Rate rises with surface area, temperature, concentration and catalysts. One thicker piece has a smaller surface area, so the rate falls.

questions.stem: Two sealed vessels contain identical initial mixtures for a reversible reaction at the same constant temperature. Only vessel X has a catalyst. A graph of product concentration against time levels off sooner for X. Which other feature should the graphs show?

options.label: A
options.text: They should level off at the same product concentration.

options.label: B
options.text: X should level off at twice the product concentration of the uncatalysed vessel.

options.label: C
options.text: X should level off at a lower product concentration.

options.label: D
options.text: The uncatalysed vessel should never form any product.

options.label: E
options.text: The uncatalysed vessel should reach equilibrium first.

options.label: F
options.text: The catalyst should change the initial product concentration.

questions.explanation: A catalyst increases both the forward and reverse rates, so the mixture reaches equilibrium sooner without changing the equilibrium composition.

questions.stem:
Use the bond energies to find the enthalpy change for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl.

H–H: 436 kJ/mol; Cl–Cl: 242 kJ/mol; H–Cl: 431 kJ/mol
questions.explanation: Bonds broken: 436 + 242 = 678 (endothermic). Bonds made: 2 × 431 = 862 (exothermic). ΔH = 678 − 862 = −184 kJ/mol. (−247 forgets that two H–Cl bonds form.)

questions.stem:
When 0.025 mol of a metal reacts with 50 cm³ of acid in an insulated cup, the temperature of the solution rises by 6.0 °C.

What is the enthalpy change per mole of metal?

(Assume the solution has density 1.0 g/cm³ and specific heat capacity 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: q = mcΔT = 50 × 4.2 × 6.0 = 1260 J = 1.26 kJ. Per mole: 1.26/0.025 = 50.4 kJ/mol. The temperature rose, so the reaction is exothermic: ΔH = −50.4 kJ/mol.

questions.stem:
Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes.

What is produced at each electrode?
questions.explanation: At the cathode, H⁺ from water is discharged rather than the more reactive Na⁺, giving H₂. At the anode, concentrated Cl⁻ is discharged to give Cl₂. Sodium hydroxide is left in solution.

questions.stem: Molten aluminium oxide is electrolysed. Which half-equation shows the reaction at the cathode?
questions.explanation: The cathode is negative; cations gain electrons there (reduction): Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. Oxide ions are oxidised at the anode.

questions.stem:
Dodecane is cracked: C₁₂H₂₆ → C₈H₁₈ + 2X

What is X?
questions.explanation: Atoms left for 2X: C 12 − 8 = 4 and H 26 − 18 = 8, so X = C₂H₄ (ethene).

questions.stem: Which compound is formed when but-2-ene reacts with steam in the presence of a catalyst?
questions.explanation: Steam adds H and OH across the C=C double bond. In CH₃CH=CHCH₃ both double-bond carbons are C2/C3, so the product is CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, butan-2-ol.

questions.stem:
Ethanol reacts with propanoic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst to form an ester and water.

What is the relative formula mass of the ester?

(Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH (46) + C₂H₅COOH (74) → C₂H₅COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (18). Ester Mr = 46 + 74 − 18 = 102 (C₅H₁₀O₂, ethyl propanoate).

questions.stem:
A solution of an unknown salt gives a brown precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide. Another sample gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution in the presence of dilute hydrochloric acid.

What is the salt?
questions.explanation: Brown hydroxide precipitate → Fe³⁺ (Fe²⁺ gives green, Cu²⁺ blue). White precipitate with acidified BaCl₂ → sulfate.

questions.stem:
A car travelling at 30 m/s brakes with uniform deceleration and stops in a distance of 45 m.

How long does it take to stop?
questions.explanation: v² − u² = 2as gives 0 − 900 = 2a × 45, so a = −10 m/s². Time = 30 ÷ 10 = 3.0 s. (Or: average speed 15 m/s over 45 m.)

questions.stem:
A trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving at 3.0 m/s collides with a stationary trolley of mass 1.0 kg. The trolleys stick together.

How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
questions.explanation: Momentum: 2 × 3 = 3v, so v = 2.0 m/s. KE before = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J; after = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 J. Loss = 3.0 J.

questions.stem:
Two 6.0 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. This combination is connected in series with a 3.0 Ω resistor across a 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance.

What is the power dissipated in ONE of the 6.0 Ω resistors?
questions.explanation: Parallel pair = 3.0 Ω, total = 6.0 Ω, so the battery current is 2.0 A. It splits equally: 1.0 A through each 6.0 Ω resistor. P = I²R = 1² × 6 = 6.0 W.

questions.stem:
A diver is 15 m below the surface of the sea. Atmospheric pressure is 100 kPa.

What is the total pressure on the diver?

(density of seawater = 1000 kg/m³; g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure = hρg = 15 × 1000 × 10 = 150 000 Pa = 150 kPa. Add atmospheric pressure: 250 kPa.

questions.stem:
A ship sends a sonar pulse straight down. The echo from the seabed is received 0.80 s after the pulse is sent.

The speed of sound in seawater is 1500 m/s. How deep is the sea?
questions.explanation: The pulse travels 1500 × 0.80 = 1200 m in total, down and back. Depth = 600 m.

questions.stem:
The activity of a radioactive sample falls from 3200 Bq to 200 Bq in 36 hours.

What is the half-life?

A nucleus of uranium-238 (atomic number 92) undergoes four decays in this order: alpha, beta-minus, beta-minus, alpha.

What are the mass number and atomic number of the final nucleus?
questions.explanation: Each alpha: mass −4, atomic number −2. Each beta-minus: mass unchanged, atomic number +1. Mass: 238 − 8 = 230. Atomic number: 92 − 4 + 2 = 90.

questions.stem:
A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. It bounces and rises to a maximum height of 12.8 m. Air resistance is negligible.

What is the speed of the ball just after it leaves the ground?

(g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: After the bounce, KE becomes GPE: v² = 2gh = 2 × 10 × 12.8 = 256, so v = 16 m/s. (It hits the ground at 20 m/s.)

questions.stem:
A lift of total mass 800 kg is accelerating upwards at 1.5 m/s².

What is the tension in the lift cable?

(g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: Resultant force = T − mg = ma, so T = m(g + a) = 800 × 11.5 = 9200 N.

questions.stem:
A spring obeys Hooke's law. It stores 0.60 J of elastic energy when its extension is 4.0 cm.

How much energy does it store when its extension is 6.0 cm? (The limit of proportionality is not exceeded.)
questions.explanation: E = ½kx², so E ∝ x². Energy = 0.60 × (6/4)² = 0.60 × 2.25 = 1.35 J. (0.90 J assumes E ∝ x.)

questions.stem:
A 2.0 kW electric kettle heats 2.0 kg of water from 20 °C to 70 °C. 70% of the electrical energy supplied heats the water.

How long does this take?

(specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Energy to water = mcΔθ = 2 × 4200 × 50 = 420 000 J. Useful power = 0.7 × 2000 = 1400 W. Time = 420 000 ÷ 1400 = 300 s.

questions.stem:
0.50 kg of ice at 0 °C is melted by a 500 W heater. All of the heater's energy goes into the ice.

How long does it take for all the ice to melt?

(specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.3 × 10⁵ J/kg)

A fixed mass of gas occupies 3.0 litres at a pressure of 100 kPa. It is compressed slowly to 1.2 litres at constant temperature.

What is its new pressure?
questions.explanation: pV = constant: 100 × 3.0 = p × 1.2, so p = 250 kPa.

questions.stem:
An ideal transformer has 800 turns on its primary coil. It steps 240 V down to 12 V and supplies a current of 3.0 A from its secondary coil.

How many turns are on the secondary coil, and what is the current in the primary coil?
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np: Ns = 800 × 12/240 = 40. Power in = power out: 240 × Ip = 12 × 3.0, so Ip = 0.15 A.

questions.stem:
A horizontal wire of length 0.20 m and mass 2.0 g lies at right angles to a horizontal uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.50 T.

What current in the wire would make the magnetic force on it equal in size to its weight?

(g = 10 N/kg)

Light travels from air into glass, entering at an angle to the normal.

Which row describes what happens to the light as it enters the glass?

options.label: A
options.text: speed decreases; wavelength decreases; frequency unchanged; bends away from the normal

options.label: B
options.text: speed increases; wavelength increases; frequency unchanged; bends away from the normal

options.label: C
options.text: speed unchanged; wavelength decreases; frequency increases; bends towards the normal

options.label: D
options.text: speed increases; wavelength decreases; frequency unchanged; bends towards the normal

options.label: E
options.text: speed decreases; wavelength unchanged; frequency decreases; bends towards the normal

options.label: F
options.text: speed decreases; wavelength decreases; frequency unchanged; bends towards the normal

questions.explanation: Frequency is set by the source and never changes on refraction. Glass is optically denser, so the light slows; v = fλ means λ falls; slowing bends it towards the normal.

questions.stem: Which list puts these electromagnetic waves in order of INCREASING frequency?

options.label: A
options.text: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma

options.label: B
options.text: radio, microwaves, visible, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma

options.label: C
options.text: microwaves, radio, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, gamma, X-rays

options.label: D
options.text: radio, infrared, microwaves, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma

options.label: E
options.text: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, X-rays, ultraviolet, gamma

options.label: F
options.text: gamma, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio

questions.explanation: Frequency rises (and wavelength falls) from radio through microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet and X-rays to gamma.

questions.stem: A supply transfers 24 J as 4 C flows through lamp X. A different supply transfers the same energy to lamp Y while 8 C flows. What is the potential difference across Y compared with X?
questions.explanation: Potential difference is energy per unit charge. The same energy divided by twice the charge gives half the potential difference.

questions.stem:
An NTC thermistor and a fixed resistor are connected in series across a battery. A voltmeter is connected across the fixed resistor.

The temperature of the thermistor rises. What happens?

options.label: A
options.text: The thermistor's resistance falls and the voltmeter reading rises.

options.label: B
options.text: The thermistor's resistance rises and the voltmeter reading rises.

options.label: C
options.text: The thermistor's resistance falls and the voltmeter reading is unchanged.

options.label: D
options.text: The thermistor's resistance falls and the voltmeter reading falls.

options.label: E
options.text: The thermistor's resistance rises and the voltmeter reading falls.

options.label: F
options.text: The thermistor's resistance is unchanged and the voltmeter reading rises.

questions.explanation: NTC: resistance falls as temperature rises. The thermistor takes a smaller share of the battery voltage, so the fixed resistor's share (the voltmeter reading) rises.

questions.stem:
A ball of mass 0.20 kg hits a wall at 15 m/s and rebounds along the same line at 10 m/s. It is in contact with the wall for 0.050 s.

What is the average force exerted on the ball by the wall?
questions.explanation: Velocity changes from +15 to −10 m/s: a change of 25 m/s. Δp = 0.20 × 25 = 5.0 kg m/s. F = Δp/Δt = 5.0 ÷ 0.050 = 100 N. (20 N wrongly uses 15 − 10 = 5 m/s.)

questions.stem:
An electric crane lifts a load of mass 500 kg through a height of 12 m in 20 s at constant speed. The crane is 60% efficient.

What is the electrical input power of the crane?

(g = 10 N/kg)

An ambulance with its siren sounding moves towards a stationary observer at constant speed.

Compared with the sound heard when the ambulance is stationary, the sound the observer hears has:

options.label: A
options.text: a higher frequency and a longer wavelength

options.label: B
options.text: a higher frequency and a shorter wavelength

options.label: C
options.text: a lower frequency and a shorter wavelength

options.label: D
options.text: a lower frequency and a longer wavelength

options.label: E
options.text: the same frequency and a shorter wavelength

options.label: F
options.text: the same frequency and the same wavelength

questions.explanation: The Doppler effect: wavefronts bunch up ahead of a moving source, so the observer receives a shorter wavelength and, since the speed of sound is unchanged, a higher frequency.

questions.stem:
A beam containing alpha particles, beta-minus particles and gamma rays passes through a uniform magnetic field at right angles to the field.

Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Gamma rays are deflected most because they have the highest energy.

options.label: B
options.text: All three are deflected, with gamma rays deflected least.

options.label: C
options.text: Beta particles are deflected more than alpha particles, in the same direction; gamma rays are not deflected.

options.label: D
options.text: Beta particles are deflected more than alpha particles, in the opposite direction; gamma rays are not deflected.

options.label: E
options.text: Alpha particles are deflected more than beta particles, in the opposite direction; gamma rays are not deflected.

options.label: F
options.text: Only alpha particles are deflected because only they are charged.

questions.explanation: Alpha (+2) and beta-minus (−1) have opposite charges so curve opposite ways. Beta particles have far smaller mass, so they are deflected much more. Gamma rays are uncharged.

questions.stem:
A bar magnet is pushed into a coil connected to a sensitive voltmeter, and a voltage is induced.

Which change would NOT increase the size of the induced voltage?

options.label: A
options.text: using a coil with more turns

options.label: B
options.text: using a coil with the same number of turns wound more tightly around an iron core

options.label: C
options.text: pushing two identical magnets in side by side, like poles together

options.label: F
options.text: reversing the magnet so the other pole enters first

questions.explanation: Induced voltage depends on how fast the flux linkage changes: speed, field strength and number of turns (an iron core also strengthens the field). Reversing the magnet only reverses the direction of the voltage.

questions.stem:
Four identical metal cans contain equal masses of hot water at the same temperature. The outside of each can has a different surface. They cool in the same room.

Which can cools fastest by thermal radiation?

options.label: C
options.text: it depends only on the room temperature

options.label: F
options.text: all cool at the same rate

questions.explanation: Dark, matt surfaces are the best emitters (and absorbers) of infrared radiation; light, shiny surfaces are the worst.

questions.stem:
1.5 kg of metal X (density 7.5 g/cm³) is mixed with 0.90 kg of metal Y (density 3.0 g/cm³) to make an alloy. Assume the volume of the alloy equals the total volume of the two metals.

What is the density of the alloy?
questions.explanation: Volumes: 1500 ÷ 7.5 = 200 cm³ and 900 ÷ 3.0 = 300 cm³. Density = 2400 g ÷ 500 cm³ = 4.8 g/cm³. (5.25 is the trap of averaging the densities.)

questions.stem:
A power station sends 100 kW along cables of total resistance 5.0 Ω at a transmission voltage of 10 kV.

What percentage of the transmitted power is lost as heat in the cables?
questions.explanation: Current = P/V = 100 000 ÷ 10 000 = 10 A. Loss = I²R = 100 × 5 = 500 W, which is 0.5% of 100 kW. (Do not use V²/R with the transmission voltage: most of that voltage is not across the cables.)

questions.stem:
The polynomial f(x) = x³ − 2x² + ax + 6 has (x − 3) as a factor.

What is the value of a?
questions.explanation: Factor theorem: f(3) = 27 − 18 + 3a + 6 = 0, so 3a = −15 and a = −5.

questions.stem:
An arithmetic sequence has first term 3 and common difference 4.

What is the sum of its first 20 terms?

A geometric series has first term 12 and sum to infinity 48.

What is the common ratio?
What is the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 + x)⁵?
questions.explanation: The x³ term is ⁵C₃ × 2² × x³ = 10 × 4 = 40.

questions.stem: Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.
questions.explanation: Complete the square: (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25. Centre (3, −2), radius 5.

questions.stem: How many solutions does 2sin²x = sin x have in the interval 0 ≤ x < 2π?
questions.explanation: sin x(2sin x − 1) = 0. sin x = 0 gives x = 0, π (2π is excluded). sin x = 1/2 gives π/6, 5π/6. Total 4. Do not divide by sin x: that loses solutions.

questions.stem:
Angle θ is obtuse and sin θ = 3/5.

What is the value of tan θ?
Solve log₂x + log₂(x − 2) = 3.
questions.explanation: log₂[x(x − 2)] = 3, so x² − 2x = 8 and (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0. x = −2 is rejected because log₂x needs x > 0. x = 4.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all real solutions of 4ˣ − 3 × 2ˣ⁺¹ + 8 = 0?
questions.explanation: Let y = 2ˣ: 4ˣ = y² and 3 × 2ˣ⁺¹ = 6y. y² − 6y + 8 = 0 gives y = 2 or 4, so x = 1 or 2. Sum = 3.

questions.stem: Find the y-coordinate of the local maximum of y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 1.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x − 1)(x − 3). d²y/dx² = 6x − 12 is negative at x = 1, so the maximum is at x = 1: y = 1 − 6 + 9 + 1 = 5.

questions.stem:
The tangent to y = x² + 3x at the point where x = 1 meets the y-axis at P.

What is the y-coordinate of P?
questions.explanation: At x = 1, y = 4 and dy/dx = 2x + 3 = 5. Tangent: y − 4 = 5(x − 1), so y = 5x − 1. P = (0, −1).

questions.stem: Find the area of the region enclosed by y = x² and y = 2x.
questions.explanation: They meet at x = 0 and x = 2. Area = ∫₀² (2x − x²) dx = [x² − x³/3]₀² = 4 − 8/3 = 4/3.

questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₁⁴ (3√x − 2/x²) dx.

The point (1, 5) lies on the curve y = f(x).

Which point must lie on the curve y = 2f(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: x − 3 = 1 means x = 4 (translation +3 in x). The y-value is doubled: 10.

questions.stem: Solve the inequality x² − 5x + 4 < 0.
questions.explanation: (x − 1)(x − 4) < 0. The parabola opens upwards, so it is negative between its roots: 1 < x < 4.

questions.stem: For which values of k does kx² + 4x + k = 0 have no real roots?
questions.explanation: Discriminant 16 − 4k² < 0 means k² > 4: k < −2 or k > 2. (For k = 0 the equation is 4x = 0, which has a root.)

questions.stem: A student uses cos²x = 1 − sin²x to turn an equation into (2sin x − 1)(2sin x + 3) = 0. They say both factors give solutions in 0 ≤ x < 2π. Which statement corrects their argument?

options.label: A
options.text: Only 2sin x − 1 = 0 gives solutions, and it gives one.

options.label: B
options.text: Only 2sin x + 3 = 0 gives solutions, and it gives two.

options.label: D
options.text: Both factors give two solutions each.

options.label: E
options.text: Both factors give one solution each.

options.label: F
options.text: Only 2sin x − 1 = 0 gives solutions, and it gives two.

questions.explanation: The second factor requires sin x = −3/2, outside the range [−1, 1]. The first gives sin x = 1/2, true at π/6 and 5π/6.

questions.stem:
A sequence is defined by u₁ = 3 and uₙ₊₁ = 2uₙ − 1.

What is u₅?
What is the value of Σ (2r + 1) for r = 1 to 10?

Line L passes through (1, 2) and is perpendicular to 2x + 3y = 6.

Where does L cross the y-axis?
questions.explanation: 2x + 3y = 6 has gradient −2/3, so L has gradient 3/2. y − 2 = (3/2)(x − 1); at x = 0, y = 2 − 3/2 = 1/2.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the stationary points of y = x⁴ − 4x³?

options.label: A
options.text: a minimum at x = 0 and a maximum at x = 3

options.label: B
options.text: a stationary point of inflection at x = 3 and a minimum at x = 0

options.label: C
options.text: a maximum at x = 0 and a minimum at x = 3

options.label: E
options.text: only one stationary point, a minimum at x = 3

options.label: F
options.text: a minimum at x = 3 and a stationary point of inflection at x = 0

questions.explanation: dy/dx = 4x²(x − 3) = 0 at x = 0, 3. The gradient is negative on both sides of x = 0 (the x² factor does not change sign), so it is a point of inflection; it changes from − to + at x = 3, a minimum.

questions.stem: Given that logₐ2 = p and logₐ3 = q, which expression equals logₐ12?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3, so logₐ12 = 2logₐ2 + logₐ3 = 2p + q.

questions.stem:
A colony of 500 bacteria doubles in number every 3 hours.

After how many hours does it first reach 64 000?

A curve has gradient dy/dx = 6x² − 2x and passes through (1, 4).

What is y when x = 2?
How many points of intersection do the curve y = x³ − 3x and the line y = 2 have?
questions.explanation: x³ − 3x − 2 = 0 factorises as (x + 1)²(x − 2) = 0. Roots x = −1 (repeated: the line touches the curve at its local maximum) and x = 2. Two points.

questions.stem:
The line y = x + c is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 8, and c > 0.

What is c?
questions.explanation: Substitute: 2x² + 2cx + c² − 8 = 0. Tangent means discriminant zero: 4c² − 8(c² − 8) = 0, so c² = 16 and c = 4.

questions.stem: What is the greatest value of 5/(3 − 2cos²x) as x varies over all real numbers?
questions.explanation: 0 ≤ cos²x ≤ 1, so the denominator ranges from 1 to 3. The fraction is greatest when the denominator is smallest (1): 5.

questions.stem:
Some money is shared between Asha, Ben and Cara in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5.

Cara then gives a quarter of her share to Asha.

What is the new ratio Asha : Ben : Cara?
questions.explanation: Use 10 parts: Asha 2, Ben 3, Cara 5. Cara gives 5/4 = 1.25 parts, so Asha 3.25, Ben 3, Cara 3.75. Multiply by 4: 13 : 12 : 15.

questions.stem: What is the value of (√48 + √27 − √75)² ?
Which of the following is a correct factorisation of 6x² − x − 15 ?

300 ml of a drink that is 20% juice is mixed with 200 ml of a drink that is 45% juice.

How much water must be added so that the mixture is 25% juice?
questions.explanation: Juice = 0.2 × 300 + 0.45 × 200 = 60 + 90 = 150 ml. For 25% juice the total must be 150 ÷ 0.25 = 600 ml. Currently 500 ml, so add 100 ml.

questions.stem:
Line L passes through the point (2, −1) and is perpendicular to the line 3x − 4y = 12.

At which point does L cross the y-axis?
questions.explanation: 3x − 4y = 12 has gradient 3/4, so L has gradient −4/3. y + 1 = −(4/3)(x − 2). At x = 0: y = −1 + 8/3 = 5/3.

questions.stem:
In a regular polygon, the ratio of each interior angle to each exterior angle is 7 : 2.

How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Interior + exterior = 180°, so exterior = 180° × 2/9 = 40°. Exterior angles sum to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 40 = 9.

questions.stem:
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and their scores are added.

What is the probability that the total is a prime number?
questions.explanation: Prime totals: 2 (1 way), 3 (2), 5 (4), 7 (6), 11 (2). That is 15 of the 36 outcomes: 15/36 = 5/12.

questions.stem:
6 workers working at the same rate would build a wall in 10 days.

After 4 days, 3 more workers, who work at the same rate, join them.

How many days does the whole job take altogether?
questions.explanation: Total work = 60 worker-days. After 4 days, 24 are done, leaving 36. With 9 workers that takes 4 more days, so 8 days in total.

questions.stem:
A rectangle has length (x + 3) cm and width (x − 1) cm. Its area is 32 cm².

What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: (x + 3)(x − 1) = 32 → x² + 2x − 35 = 0 → (x + 7)(x − 5) = 0. Lengths must be positive, so x = 5: sides 8 and 4, perimeter 24 cm.

questions.stem:
The space diagonal of a cube (from one vertex to the opposite vertex, through the cube) is 6 cm long.

What is the total surface area of the cube?
questions.explanation: For side a, the space diagonal is √(3a²) = a√3 = 6, so a² = 12. Surface area = 6a² = 72 cm².

questions.stem:
A trapezium has parallel sides of length x cm and (x + 6) cm. The perpendicular distance between them is (x − 1) cm. The area of the trapezium is 21 cm².

What is the length of the longer parallel side?
Five sensor readings have mean 8. A sixth reading is added. The mean of all six readings is also 8. What is the sixth reading?
questions.explanation: The total rises from 5 × 8 to 6 × 8, so the added reading is 8.

questions.stem:
A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. A field covers an area of 12 cm² on the map.

What is the real area of the field?
questions.explanation: 1 cm on the map is 250 m, so 1 cm² is 250 × 250 = 62 500 m². 12 cm² is 750 000 m² = 0.75 km². (3 km² comes from scaling the area by the length factor only.)

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of √(0.0491 × 812) ÷ 0.198 ?

A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. The tangent to the circle at A makes an angle of 64° with the chord AB. C lies on the major arc AB.

What is the size of angle OAB?
questions.explanation: The angle between a radius and a tangent is 90°, so angle OAB = 90° − 64° = 26°. (Check: by the alternate segment theorem ACB = 64°, so AOB = 128° and the isosceles triangle OAB has base angles 26°.)

questions.stem:
There are 40 students in a year group. 23 study French, 18 study Spanish and 7 study neither.

A student who studies Spanish is chosen at random. What is the probability that this student also studies French?
questions.explanation: 33 students study at least one language, so the number studying both is 23 + 18 − 33 = 8. Given Spanish, the probability is 8/18 = 4/9.

questions.stem: What is the value of 2 − 3 × (−2)² ÷ 6 + (−1)³ ?
questions.explanation: Powers first: (−2)² = 4 and (−1)³ = −1. Then 3 × 4 ÷ 6 = 2. So 2 − 2 − 1 = −1.

questions.stem:
Money is invested at 4% per year simple interest. After 5 years the total value of the investment is £3600.

How much was originally invested?
questions.explanation: Simple interest adds 5 × 4% = 20% of the original, so 1.2P = 3600 and P = £3000. (£2880 is the mistake of taking 20% off £3600.)

questions.stem: Given that (x + a)² + b ≡ x² − 10x + 7 for all x, what is the value of a + b ?

The point P(3, −2) is reflected in the line y = x. The image is then rotated 90° clockwise about the origin.

What are the coordinates of the final image?
questions.explanation: Reflection in y = x swaps coordinates: (−2, 3). A 90° clockwise rotation maps (x, y) to (y, −x): (3, 2). The combination is the same as a reflection in the x-axis.

questions.stem: How many solutions does the equation sin x = 0.3 have for 0° ≤ x ≤ 720° ?
questions.explanation: In each 360° cycle, sin x = 0.3 has two solutions (one in (0°, 90°) and one in (90°, 180°)). Two full cycles give 4 solutions.

questions.stem:
In a club the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. When 12 more boys join, the ratio becomes 1 : 1.

How many members did the club have before the boys joined?
questions.explanation: Boys 3k, girls 5k. 3k + 12 = 5k gives k = 6, so there were 18 boys and 30 girls: 48 members.

questions.stem: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (7, 4) and (3, 8) ?
questions.explanation: Enclose it in the rectangle 1 ≤ x ≤ 7, 2 ≤ y ≤ 8 (area 36) and subtract three right triangles: ½×6×2 = 6, ½×4×4 = 8, ½×2×6 = 6. 36 − 20 = 16.

questions.stem:
A number x is truncated to 1 decimal place. The result is 3.7.

Which of the following is the error interval for x?
questions.explanation: Truncation cuts off digits after the first decimal place, so any x from 3.7 up to (but not including) 3.8 truncates to 3.7. 3.65 ≤ x < 3.75 is the interval for rounding.

questions.stem:
A scatter graph shows strong positive correlation between daily ice cream sales and the number of cases of sunburn treated at a clinic.

Which conclusion is justified by the graph alone?

options.label: B
options.text: Ice cream sales and sunburn cases are always equal.

options.label: C
options.text: There is no relationship between the two variables.

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing ice cream sales would reduce sunburn.

options.label: E
options.text: Days with higher ice cream sales tend to have more sunburn cases.

options.label: F
options.text: Sunburn causes people to buy ice cream.

questions.explanation: Correlation shows the variables tend to rise together; it does not show causation. Both are probably driven by a third factor: sunny weather.

questions.stem:
The probability that it rains today is 0.3. If it rains today, the probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.6. If it does not rain today, the probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.2.

What is the probability that it rains on exactly one of the two days?
questions.explanation: Rain then dry: 0.3 × 0.4 = 0.12. Dry then rain: 0.7 × 0.2 = 0.14. Total 0.26.

questions.stem:
2 adult tickets and 3 child tickets cost £39. 3 adult tickets and 2 child tickets cost £46.

How much do 1 adult ticket and 4 child tickets cost?
questions.explanation: Adding: 5a + 5c = 85, so a + c = 17. Subtracting: a − c = 7. So a = 12 and c = 5, and a + 4c = £32.

questions.stem: Which structure is found in both plant and animal cells but NOT in bacterial cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria occur in eukaryotic cells (plant and animal) but not prokaryotes. Bacteria have membranes, cytoplasm, cell walls and plasmids; chloroplasts are plant-only.

questions.stem: Which list is in order of increasing level of organisation?
questions.explanation: Similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together as organ systems.

questions.stem:
Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from soil water in which the ions are at a lower concentration than inside the cells.

Which process is used, and what does it require?

options.label: B
options.text: active transport, requiring energy from respiration

questions.explanation: Moving ions against a concentration gradient is active transport, which uses carrier proteins and energy from respiration (so root cells have many mitochondria).

questions.stem: A cell with 8 chromosomes divides by mitosis. Immediately before mitosis begins (after DNA replication in interphase), how many DNA molecules does it contain?
questions.explanation: Each of the 8 chromosomes has been copied into two identical chromatids, giving 16 DNA molecules. Each daughter cell receives 8.

questions.stem: Which statement about asexual reproduction is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: It involves meiosis to produce gametes.

options.label: C
options.text: It always produces more variation than sexual reproduction.

options.label: E
options.text: It involves one parent, and the offspring are genetically identical if no mutations occur.

options.label: F
options.text: It involves two parents and produces genetically varied offspring.

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction uses mitosis from a single parent, giving clones unless mutations occur.

questions.stem:
In a species of plant, red flowers (R) are dominant to white (r). Two red-flowered plants are crossed. Of 400 offspring, about 100 have white flowers.

About how many of the red-flowered offspring are expected to be heterozygous?
questions.explanation: A 3 : 1 ratio means both parents are Rr. Offspring RR : Rr : rr = 1 : 2 : 1, so Rr ≈ 200 of the 400 (two-thirds of the 300 red plants).

questions.stem: Which statement about the inheritance of phenotypes is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Most phenotypes result from several genes, and only some result from a single gene.

options.label: B
options.text: Every gene has only two alleles in a population.

options.label: C
options.text: Phenotype is never affected by the environment.

options.label: E
options.text: Recessive alleles are always rarer than dominant ones.

options.label: F
options.text: All phenotypes are controlled by a single gene.

questions.explanation: Most characteristics, such as height, are polygenic and also affected by the environment.

questions.stem: What is the genome of an organism?

options.label: A
options.text: the DNA in one gamete only

options.label: B
options.text: the full set of its genetic material

options.label: D
options.text: the set of alleles for one characteristic

questions.explanation: The genome is all the DNA of an organism, contained within its chromosomes.

questions.stem: What does each DNA nucleotide consist of?

options.label: A
options.text: a phosphate group and an amino acid

options.label: B
options.text: a glycerol and three fatty acids

options.label: C
options.text: an amino acid, a sugar and a base

options.label: D
options.text: a sugar, a phosphate group and one of four bases

options.label: E
options.text: a base pair and a sugar

questions.explanation: A nucleotide is a sugar (deoxyribose) joined to a phosphate group and one nitrogenous base: A, T, G or C.

questions.stem: A mutation replaces one amino acid in an enzyme with another, and the enzyme stops working. What is the most likely reason?

options.label: A
options.text: The DNA can no longer be replicated.

options.label: B
options.text: The enzyme can no longer be transported in the blood.

options.label: C
options.text: The enzyme now has no amino acids.

options.label: D
options.text: The enzyme has been denatured by heat.

options.label: E
options.text: The mutation changed every amino acid in the enzyme.

options.label: F
options.text: The amino acid sequence determines the protein's 3D shape, so the shape of the active site has changed.

questions.explanation: A protein folds according to its amino acid sequence. One change can alter the folding and the active site, so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.stem: Which is a RISK of using genetic engineering in medicine?

options.label: A
options.text: Genetically modified cells can produce proteins in large quantities.

options.label: C
options.text: Bacteria can be engineered to produce human insulin.

options.label: D
options.text: It allows treatment of some inherited disorders.

options.label: E
options.text: An inserted gene could have unintended effects on other genes.

options.label: F
options.text: It reduces the need to extract hormones from animals.

questions.explanation: The other options are benefits. Risks include unpredictable effects of the inserted gene, and ethical and long-term safety concerns.

questions.stem: How does selective breeding differ from natural selection?

options.label: A
options.text: Natural selection is faster than selective breeding.

options.label: B
options.text: Selective breeding produces new alleles directly.

options.label: C
options.text: Only natural selection changes allele frequencies.

options.label: D
options.text: Selective breeding does not need genetic variation.

options.label: E
options.text: Selective breeding always increases genetic variation.

options.label: F
options.text: Humans choose which individuals reproduce, rather than the environment determining survival.

questions.explanation: Both act on existing variation and change allele frequencies over generations. In selective breeding humans pick the parents; it often reduces genetic variation.

questions.stem: Identical twins raised in different countries differ in body mass. What is the best explanation?

options.label: B
options.text: one twin has an extra chromosome

options.label: D
options.text: differences in their alleles inherited from their parents

options.label: E
options.text: genetic variation from mutation in every cell

questions.explanation: Identical twins have the same alleles, so differences between them are environmental (diet, exercise).

questions.stem: Which enzyme digests fats, and what are the products?
questions.explanation: Lipase breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol. Amylase digests starch to sugars; proteases digest proteins to amino acids.

questions.stem: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water. The reverse is photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which is the correct pathway of blood from the body back to the body?

options.label: A
options.text: pulmonary vein → right atrium → right ventricle → aorta → lungs → vena cava → left atrium → left ventricle

options.label: B
options.text: vena cava → left atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → right atrium → right ventricle → aorta

options.label: C
options.text: vena cava → right ventricle → right atrium → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left ventricle → left atrium → aorta

options.label: D
options.text: vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary vein → lungs → pulmonary artery → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta

options.label: E
options.text: aorta → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary vein → lungs → pulmonary artery → left atrium → left ventricle → vena cava

options.label: F
options.text: vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta

questions.explanation: Deoxygenated blood enters the right side via the vena cava and goes to the lungs in the pulmonary artery; oxygenated blood returns in the pulmonary vein to the left side and leaves via the aorta.

questions.stem: A person’s heart pumps 60 cm³ per beat at 70 beats per minute at rest. During an activity it pumps 75 cm³ per beat at 84 beats per minute. By what factor does the volume pumped per minute increase?
questions.explanation: The volume per minute is the volume per beat multiplied by beats per minute. The ratio is (75/60) × (84/70) = (5/4) × (6/5) = 3/2.

questions.stem: Why do large multicellular animals need specialised gas exchange surfaces and a transport system?

options.label: A
options.text: They have too few cells to exchange gases.

options.label: B
options.text: Diffusion is faster over long distances.

options.label: C
options.text: Their surface area to volume ratio is large, so they lose too much water.

options.label: D
options.text: Their surface area to volume ratio is small, so diffusion across the body surface is too slow to supply all cells.

options.label: F
options.text: Oxygen cannot diffuse through cell membranes.

questions.explanation: As size increases, volume grows faster than surface area, and diffusion distances become too long, so lungs, gills and circulation are needed.

questions.stem: Where are the products of digestion mainly absorbed into the blood?
questions.explanation: The small intestine has villi giving a huge surface area, a good blood supply and thin walls for absorption. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.

questions.stem: In a healthy kidney, which substance is normally present in the filtrate in the nephron but absent from the urine?
questions.explanation: Glucose is filtered and then completely reabsorbed. Proteins and blood cells are too large to be filtered at all; urea, water and salts appear in urine.

questions.stem: Which statement about type 1 diabetes is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is caused by eating too much sugar, and it is treated with antibiotics.

options.label: B
options.text: Body cells stop responding to insulin, and it is treated mainly by diet.

options.label: C
options.text: The pancreas produces little or no insulin, and it is treated with insulin injections.

options.label: D
options.text: The liver produces too much insulin.

options.label: E
options.text: It is always caused by obesity.

options.label: F
options.text: The pancreas produces too much glucagon, and it is treated by surgery.

questions.explanation: In type 1 the insulin-secreting cells do not work, so insulin must be injected. Type 2 involves cells becoming resistant to insulin and is linked to lifestyle.

questions.stem: Which effect is caused by adrenaline?

options.label: E
options.text: increased storage of glycogen in the liver

questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for 'fight or flight': faster heart and breathing rates and more glucose released into the blood.

questions.stem: Which treatment of cardiovascular disease is a surgical procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: inserting a stent into a narrowed coronary artery

options.label: D
options.text: taking statins to reduce blood cholesterol

questions.explanation: Stents and bypass surgery are surgical; statins, anticoagulants and anti-hypertensives are medication; the others are lifestyle changes.

questions.stem:
Clover plants have bacteria in their root nodules. The bacteria supply the plant with nitrogen compounds, and the plant supplies the bacteria with sugars.

What type of relationship is this?

options.label: E
options.text: commensalism where only the plant benefits

questions.explanation: Both organisms benefit, so it is mutualism. In parasitism one benefits at the other's expense.

questions.stem: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere from dead organisms?
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead material and respire, releasing CO₂. Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from the air.

questions.stem: Fertiliser runs off farmland into a lake. Which sequence describes eutrophication?

options.label: A
options.text: plants grow rapidly → oxygen increases → fish die from too much oxygen

options.label: B
options.text: algae die → oxygen increases → fish multiply

options.label: C
options.text: algae grow rapidly → light is blocked → plants die → bacteria decompose them and use up oxygen → fish die

options.label: D
options.text: bacteria die → algae grow → oxygen increases

options.label: E
options.text: fish die → algae grow → oxygen increases

options.label: F
options.text: fertiliser kills fish directly → algae die

questions.explanation: Extra nitrates and phosphates cause algal blooms. Plants beneath die; decomposing bacteria respire and deplete oxygen, killing fish and lowering biodiversity.

questions.stem: Which statement about xylem and phloem is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Both xylem and phloem carry water only upwards.

options.label: B
options.text: Xylem consists of living cells carrying sugars; phloem consists of dead cells carrying water.

options.label: C
options.text: Phloem is made of lignified dead cells.

options.label: D
options.text: Xylem consists of lignified dead cells carrying water and minerals upwards; phloem consists of living cells carrying dissolved sugars to all parts of the plant.

options.label: E
options.text: Xylem carries sugars downwards only; phloem carries water upwards only.

options.label: F
options.text: Xylem carries dissolved sugars from the leaves to the roots.

questions.explanation: Xylem: dead, lignified, hollow tubes for water and mineral ions from roots to leaves. Phloem: living cells for translocation of sugars both up and down.

questions.stem:
Boron has two isotopes, ¹⁰B and ¹¹B. Its relative atomic mass is 10.8.

What percentage of boron atoms are ¹⁰B?

An atom has the electron configuration 2,8,6.

In which Period and Group of the Periodic Table is it found?
questions.explanation: Three occupied shells → Period 3. Six outer electrons → Group 16 (IUPAC numbering). It is sulfur.

questions.stem: Which statement about trends in reactivity is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Reactivity is the same for all elements in a group.

options.label: B
options.text: Reactivity decreases down both Group 1 and Group 17.

options.label: C
options.text: Reactivity decreases down Group 1 and increases down Group 17.

options.label: D
options.text: Reactivity increases down Group 1 and decreases down Group 17.

options.label: E
options.text: Reactivity increases down both Group 1 and Group 17.

questions.explanation: Down Group 1 the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more easily lost. Down Group 17 an extra electron is gained less easily. Group 18 is unreactive.

questions.stem:
Butane burns completely in oxygen: __C₄H₁₀ + __O₂ → __CO₂ + __H₂O

When the equation is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: Per C₄H₁₀: 4CO₂ + 5H₂O needs 13 O atoms = 6.5 O₂. Doubling for whole numbers: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O.

questions.stem:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)   ΔH = −92 kJ/mol

Which change would shift the position of equilibrium to the right?

options.label: C
options.text: adding an inert gas at constant volume

questions.explanation: The right side has fewer gas molecules (2 vs 4), so higher pressure favours it. The forward reaction is exothermic, so higher temperature shifts it left. Catalysts do not move equilibrium.

questions.stem:
What mass of iron could be extracted from 1.0 tonne of pure iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃?

(Ar: O = 16, Fe = 56)
questions.explanation: Mr Fe₂O₃ = 160, containing 2 × 56 = 112 of iron. Fraction iron = 112/160 = 0.70, so 0.70 tonnes.

questions.stem:
What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃?

(Ar: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Mr = 14 + 4 + 14 + 48 = 80. There are two N atoms: 28/80 = 35%.

questions.stem:
4.0 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm³ of solution.

What is the concentration of the solution?

(Ar: H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.explanation: Mr NaOH = 40, so 0.10 mol. Concentration = 0.10 ÷ 0.250 dm³ = 0.40 mol/dm³.

questions.stem:
20 cm³ of a gaseous hydrocarbon burns completely in excess oxygen, forming 80 cm³ of carbon dioxide and 100 cm³ of steam. All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.

What is the formula of the hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Equal gas volumes contain equal numbers of moles. 1 molecule gives 80/20 = 4 CO₂ (4 C) and 100/20 = 5 H₂O (10 H): C₄H₁₀.

questions.stem:
How many atoms are there in 0.50 mol of water molecules, H₂O?

(Avogadro constant = 6.0 × 10²³ per mol)
questions.explanation: 0.50 mol of molecules = 3.0 × 10²³ molecules, each with 3 atoms: 9.0 × 10²³ atoms.

questions.stem: Which reaction does NOT involve oxidation or reduction?
questions.explanation: In CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ every oxidation state stays the same (Ca +2, C +4, O −2). All the others involve electron transfer (H₂O₂ disproportionates).

questions.stem: Which statement about graphite is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds to other carbon atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: It conducts electricity because each carbon atom has one delocalised electron.

options.label: C
options.text: It conducts electricity because it contains free ions.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a simple molecular substance.

options.label: E
options.text: It has a low melting point because the forces between its layers are weak.

options.label: F
options.text: It is hard because its layers cannot slide.

questions.explanation: In graphite each C bonds to three others in layers, leaving one delocalised electron per atom to carry charge. Melting requires breaking strong covalent bonds, so its melting point is very high; weak forces between layers only make it soft.

questions.stem: Why do the boiling points of straight-chain alkanes increase as the chain gets longer?

options.label: B
options.text: More covalent bonds must be broken to boil the alkane.

options.label: D
options.text: Longer molecules have more double bonds.

options.label: E
options.text: The intermolecular forces between the molecules get stronger.

options.label: F
options.text: The covalent bonds within the molecules get stronger.

questions.explanation: Boiling a simple molecular substance overcomes intermolecular forces only. Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces. No covalent bonds break on boiling.

questions.stem: Why are solid metals good electrical conductors?

options.label: A
options.text: They contain positive ions that can move through the structure.

options.label: B
options.text: Their atoms are arranged in layers that slide.

options.label: D
options.text: They contain delocalised electrons that can move through the structure.

options.label: E
options.text: Their atoms are held by strong covalent bonds.

questions.explanation: A metal is a lattice of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons; the electrons move when a voltage is applied. The ions stay fixed.

questions.stem:
4.0 g of copper(II) oxide reacts completely with excess dilute sulfuric acid:
CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O

What mass of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate could be obtained?

(Ar: O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 63.5)
questions.explanation: Mr CuO = 79.5, so 4.0 g ≈ 0.050 mol. CuSO₄ has Mr 159.5: 0.050 × 159.5 ≈ 7.98 g. (It is the 1 : 1 ratio that matters, not the mass of acid.)

questions.stem: Which oxide reacts with water to form an alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Metal oxides such as Na₂O form hydroxides (Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH). Non-metal oxides form acids, except SiO₂, which is insoluble.

questions.stem:
0.12 g of magnesium ribbon reacts with excess hydrochloric acid and the volume of hydrogen is measured against time. The experiment is repeated with the same mass of magnesium and the same volume of acid at half the concentration (the acid is still in excess).

How does the second experiment compare with the first?

options.label: A
options.text: The initial rate is lower and the final volume is doubled.

options.label: B
options.text: The initial rate is lower and the final volume of hydrogen is halved.

options.label: C
options.text: The initial rate is higher and the final volume is the same.

options.label: D
options.text: Both the initial rate and the final volume are unchanged.

options.label: E
options.text: The initial rate is the same and the final volume is halved.

options.label: F
options.text: The initial rate is lower and the final volume of hydrogen is the same.

questions.explanation: The magnesium is limiting in both experiments, so the same amount of hydrogen forms (0.005 mol, 120 cm³ at rtp). Lower acid concentration means fewer collisions per second, so a lower initial rate.

questions.stem: The reactants of an exothermic reaction are drawn at 90 kJ mol⁻¹ on an energy profile. The forward activation energy is 55 kJ mol⁻¹ and the enthalpy change of the forward reaction is −20 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the reverse activation energy?
questions.explanation: The peak is at 90 + 55 = 145 and the products at 90 − 20 = 70 kJ mol⁻¹. The reverse activation energy is 145 − 70 = 75 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem:
The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic, with ΔH = −57 kJ/mol.

What is the enthalpy change of the reverse reaction?

options.label: D
options.text: It cannot be found without the activation energy.

questions.explanation: The reverse of an exothermic reaction is endothermic by the same amount: +57 kJ/mol.

questions.stem:
Copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed using inert (graphite) electrodes.

What forms at each electrode?
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ is less reactive than hydrogen, so copper is deposited at the cathode. Sulfate is not discharged; water is oxidised at the anode to give oxygen.

questions.stem:
A steel spoon is to be electroplated with silver.

Which arrangement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: spoon as the anode; graphite as the cathode; silver nitrate solution as the electrolyte

options.label: B
options.text: spoon as the cathode; silver as the anode; silver nitrate solution as the electrolyte

options.label: C
options.text: an alternating current with the spoon and silver in silver nitrate solution

options.label: D
options.text: spoon as the anode; silver as the cathode; silver nitrate solution as the electrolyte

options.label: E
options.text: spoon as the cathode; silver as the anode; sodium chloride solution as the electrolyte

options.label: F
