options.text: spoon as the cathode; graphite as the anode; sodium chloride solution as the electrolyte

questions.explanation: Ag⁺ ions are reduced onto the object at the cathode; the silver anode dissolves to replace them. Direct current is needed, and the electrolyte must contain the plating metal's ions.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
questions.explanation: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. Other drawings are the same molecules drawn differently.

questions.stem: Which monomer forms the addition polymer with repeating unit –CH₂–CH(CH₃)– ?
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation opens the C=C bond. Putting the double bond back between the two main-chain carbons gives CH₂=CH–CH₃, propene.

questions.stem: Which statement about polyesters is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: They are formed from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid.

options.label: B
options.text: They are formed from amino acids, with water released.

options.label: C
options.text: They are addition polymers formed from monomers containing C=C bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: They are formed from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid, with no other product.

options.label: E
options.text: They are condensation polymers formed from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid, with water released.

options.label: F
options.text: They are always biodegradable because they contain ester links.

questions.explanation: Each ester link forms from –OH and –COOH with loss of H₂O, which is condensation. A diamine and dicarboxylic acid give a polyamide; amino acids give proteins.

questions.stem:
A small piece of sodium is dropped into ethanol.

What are the products?
questions.explanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. It is like sodium with water but gentler.

questions.stem:
Three metals W, X and Y are tested. X displaces both W and Y from solutions of their salts. W displaces Y from a solution of its salt.

What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?
questions.explanation: A metal only displaces a less reactive metal. X beats both; W beats Y. So X > W > Y.

questions.stem: Which pairing of a pollutant with its origin or effect is INCORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: nitrogen oxides – formed when nitrogen and oxygen react at high temperatures in engines

options.label: C
options.text: nitrogen oxides – formed mainly from sulfur impurities in fuels

options.label: D
options.text: sulfur dioxide – contributes to acid rain

options.label: E
options.text: carbon monoxide – reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen

options.label: F
options.text: carbon monoxide – produced by incomplete combustion

questions.explanation: Nitrogen oxides come from nitrogen and oxygen in the air reacting at high temperatures in engines. Sulfur impurities produce sulfur dioxide.

questions.stem:
An object accelerates uniformly from 4.0 m/s to 16 m/s in 6.0 s, then travels at 16 m/s for a further 4.0 s.

What is its average speed over the 10 s?
questions.explanation: Distance = area under the graph = ½(4 + 16) × 6 + 16 × 4 = 60 + 64 = 124 m. Average speed = 124 ÷ 10 = 12.4 m/s.

questions.stem:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 25 m/s. Air resistance is negligible.

What is the maximum height it reaches above the point of release?

(g = 10 m/s²)

A skydiver is falling at terminal velocity. She then opens her parachute.

Which describes her motion immediately afterwards and some time later?

options.label: A
options.text: Weight exceeds air resistance, so she accelerates until she reaches a higher terminal velocity.

options.label: B
options.text: Air resistance exceeds weight, so she decelerates until she reaches a new, lower terminal velocity.

options.label: C
options.text: Air resistance equals weight throughout, so her speed is constant.

options.label: D
options.text: Her weight decreases, so she slows down to a new terminal velocity.

options.label: E
options.text: Air resistance exceeds weight, so she decelerates until she comes to rest in mid-air.

options.label: F
options.text: Air resistance exceeds weight, so she moves upwards until she reaches a lower terminal velocity.

questions.explanation: Opening the parachute increases drag at the same speed, so the resultant force is upwards and she decelerates (still moving down). Drag falls as she slows until it equals her weight again: a lower terminal velocity.

questions.stem:
Blocks P (3.0 kg) and Q (2.0 kg) are in contact on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of 20 N pushes P, which pushes Q.

What is the size of the force that P exerts on Q?
questions.explanation: Both accelerate together: a = 20 ÷ 5.0 = 4.0 m/s². The only horizontal force on Q is from P: F = 2.0 × 4.0 = 8.0 N.

questions.stem:
A roller-coaster car starts from rest at the top of a track 45 m high. Friction and air resistance are negligible.

What is its speed at a point on the track 25 m above the ground?

(g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: It has dropped 20 m: ½v² = g × 20, so v² = 400 and v = 20 m/s. The mass cancels.

questions.stem:
Resistors of 2.0 Ω, 3.0 Ω and 6.0 Ω are connected in parallel across a 6.0 V battery of negligible internal resistance.

What is the current from the battery?
questions.explanation: Each resistor has the full 6.0 V across it: 6/2 = 3 A, 6/3 = 2 A, 6/6 = 1 A, total 6.0 A. (Check: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1, so R = 1.0 Ω. 0.55 A is the series answer.)

questions.stem:
The current through a filament lamp is increased steadily.

Which statement describes the lamp's V–I graph and the reason for its shape?

options.label: A
options.text: It curves so that the resistance decreases, because the filament gets hotter.

options.label: B
options.text: It curves so that the resistance increases, because the filament gets hotter.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a straight line that does not pass through the origin.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a straight line through the origin, because the filament obeys Ohm's law.

options.label: E
options.text: Current only flows when the voltage exceeds a threshold, as with a diode.

options.label: F
options.text: It curves so that the resistance increases, because the filament gets colder.

questions.explanation: As current rises the filament heats up; its ions vibrate more and resist electron flow, so the resistance (V/I) increases and the graph is not a straight line.

questions.stem:
A 2.4 kW kettle is used for 5 minutes every day for 30 days. Electricity costs 30p per kWh.

What is the cost of the electricity used?

A polythene rod becomes negatively charged when it is rubbed with a dry cloth.

Which statement explains this?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrons are transferred from the rod to the cloth.

options.label: B
options.text: Positive ions move from the rod into the cloth.

options.label: C
options.text: Protons are transferred from the rod to the cloth.

options.label: D
options.text: Electrons are transferred from the cloth to the rod.

options.label: E
options.text: Protons are transferred from the cloth to the rod.

options.label: F
options.text: Negative charge is created in the rod by friction.

questions.explanation: Charging by friction transfers electrons only; protons stay fixed in nuclei. The rod gains electrons (becomes negative) and the cloth is left equally positive.

questions.stem: A simple dc motor is spinning. Which change would make it spin in the opposite direction?

options.label: B
options.text: increasing the number of turns on the coil

options.label: D
options.text: reversing both the current and the magnetic field

options.label: F
options.text: reversing the direction of the current

questions.explanation: The force direction (left-hand rule) depends on both current and field directions. Reversing one of them reverses rotation; reversing both leaves it unchanged.

questions.stem:
12 wave crests pass a fixed point in 4.0 s. The distance between neighbouring crests is 0.50 m.

What is the speed of the waves?
questions.explanation: Frequency = 12 ÷ 4.0 = 3.0 Hz. Wavelength = 0.50 m. v = fλ = 1.5 m/s.

questions.stem:
An ultrasound scanner uses a frequency of 3.0 MHz. The speed of sound in soft tissue is 1500 m/s.

What is the wavelength of the ultrasound in soft tissue?

A ray of light strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the incident ray and the surface of the mirror is 35°.

What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
questions.explanation: Angles are measured from the normal: angle of incidence = 90° − 35° = 55°, and the reflection angle is also 55°. Angle between the rays = 110°.

questions.stem:
A sample initially contains only radioactive nuclide X, which has a half-life of 5 years and decays directly to a stable nuclide Y.

What is the ratio of Y nuclei to X nuclei after 15 years?
questions.explanation: 15 years is three half-lives, so 1/8 of X remains and 7/8 has become Y. Ratio Y : X = 7 : 1.

questions.stem: What happens in the nucleus during beta-minus decay?

options.label: A
options.text: A neutron changes into a proton and an electron is emitted; the mass number is unchanged and the atomic number increases by 1.

options.label: B
options.text: An electron from the inner shell is emitted; the atomic number is unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: A proton changes into a neutron and an electron is emitted; the mass number is unchanged and the atomic number decreases by 1.

options.label: D
options.text: Two protons and two neutrons are emitted; the mass number decreases by 4.

options.label: E
options.text: A neutron is emitted; the mass number decreases by 1.

options.label: F
options.text: A neutron changes into a proton and an electron is emitted; the mass number increases by 1.

questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay a neutron becomes a proton and a fast electron leaves the nucleus. Nucleon number stays the same; proton number rises by 1.

questions.stem:
Water is heated steadily in a kettle. While it is boiling, its temperature stays at 100 °C even though energy is still being supplied.

What is the energy being used for?

options.label: A
options.text: raising the boiling point of the water

options.label: B
options.text: increasing the average kinetic energy of the water molecules

options.label: C
options.text: heating the kettle only, not the water

options.label: D
options.text: overcoming the forces between water molecules as liquid turns to gas

options.label: E
options.text: increasing the speed of the molecules that remain in the liquid

options.label: F
options.text: breaking the covalent bonds inside water molecules

questions.explanation: During a change of state the energy (latent heat) increases the potential energy of the molecules by overcoming intermolecular forces; their average kinetic energy, and so the temperature, stays the same. The O–H bonds are not broken.

questions.stem:
Heat is conducted through a flat wall from a warm room to the cold outside.

Which change would REDUCE the rate of heat conduction through the wall?

options.label: B
options.text: increasing the temperature of the room

options.label: C
options.text: increasing the area of the wall

options.label: D
options.text: making the wall from a material with higher thermal conductivity

options.label: E
options.text: replacing the wall with a thinner metal sheet

questions.explanation: The rate of conduction increases with temperature difference, area and conductivity, and decreases with thickness.

questions.stem: Why is a room heater usually placed near the floor?

options.label: A
options.text: The floor conducts heat to the rest of the room most efficiently.

options.label: B
options.text: Heat rises because hot particles are lighter than cold particles.

options.label: C
options.text: Air near the heater warms, becomes more dense and sinks, spreading across the floor.

options.label: E
options.text: Cold air is less dense and collects near the floor.

options.label: F
options.text: Air near the heater warms, becomes less dense and rises, setting up a convection current around the room.

questions.explanation: Warm air expands and becomes less dense, so it rises; cooler, denser air sinks to replace it, circulating heat. The particles themselves do not get lighter.

questions.stem:
A uniform rectangular block measures 2.0 m × 0.50 m × 0.10 m and weighs 400 N. It can rest on any of its faces on a flat floor.

What is the greatest pressure it can exert on the floor?
questions.explanation: Greatest pressure on the smallest face: 0.50 × 0.10 = 0.050 m². p = 400 ÷ 0.050 = 8000 Pa. (The largest face gives the least, 400 Pa.)

questions.stem: Two skaters initially at rest push away from each other on level ice. One skater has twice the mass of the other. Horizontal external forces are negligible during the push. Which comparison is correct immediately after the push?

options.label: A
options.text: Their momenta are equal in magnitude and their speeds are equal.

options.label: B
options.text: Their momenta are equal in magnitude, but the heavier skater has half the speed.

options.label: C
options.text: The heavier skater has twice the momentum and the same speed.

options.label: D
options.text: The heavier skater has twice the momentum and half the speed.

options.label: E
options.text: The lighter skater has twice the momentum and twice the speed.

options.label: F
options.text: The lighter skater has half the momentum and half the speed.

questions.explanation: Their total momentum remains zero, so the individual momenta are opposite and equal in magnitude. For equal magnitude mv, doubling the mass halves the speed.

questions.stem:
A box initially at rest is pulled 8.0 m across a horizontal floor by a constant horizontal force of 50 N. A constant friction force of 30 N acts on it.

What is the kinetic energy of the box at the end?
questions.explanation: Work done by the pull = 50 × 8 = 400 J; 30 × 8 = 240 J is transferred to heat by friction. KE gained = 160 J (the work done by the 20 N resultant force).

questions.stem: Why is electricity transmitted across the National Grid at very high voltage?

options.label: A
options.text: For a given power, a higher voltage means a smaller current, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.

options.label: B
options.text: A higher voltage means a larger current, so more power reaches homes.

options.label: C
options.text: High voltage reduces the resistance of the cables.

options.label: D
options.text: High voltage makes the electricity travel faster.

options.label: E
options.text: Transformers only work at high voltage.

options.label: F
options.text: High voltage makes the cables safer to touch.

questions.explanation: P = IV, so for fixed power a higher V gives a lower I. Heating loss is I²R, so it falls sharply.

questions.stem:
Resistors R₁ = 3.0 kΩ and R₂ are connected in series across a 12 V supply. The voltage across R₂ is 4.0 V.

What is the resistance of R₂?
questions.explanation: R₁ has 12 − 4 = 8 V across it. In series the current is the same, so voltages are in the ratio of resistances: R₂ = 3.0 × 4/8 = 1.5 kΩ.

questions.stem:
An astronaut has a mass of 80 kg on Earth. The gravitational field strength on the Moon is 1.6 N/kg.

What are the astronaut's mass and weight on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass does not change with location. Weight = mg = 80 × 1.6 = 128 N.

questions.stem: Which pairing of an electromagnetic wave with a use is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Surgical instruments are sterilised with gamma rays. Microwaves are used for cooking and satellite and mobile communication.

questions.stem:
A spring has a natural length of 15 cm. When a 6.0 N weight hangs from it, its length is 18 cm.

What is its length when a 10 N weight hangs from it? (It obeys Hooke's law throughout.)
questions.explanation: Extension 3 cm for 6 N, so k = 2 N/cm. For 10 N the extension is 5 cm, so the length is 20 cm. (30 cm wrongly scales the whole length.)

questions.stem:
A car of mass 1200 kg starts from rest. The driving force is 3000 N and the total resistive force is a constant 600 N.

How far does the car travel before reaching a speed of 20 m/s?
What is the value of 8^(2/3) × 4^(−1/2)?

When f(x) = 2x³ + x² − 5x + c is divided by (x + 2), the remainder is 4.

What is c?
questions.explanation: Remainder theorem: f(−2) = −16 + 4 + 10 + c = c − 2 = 4, so c = 6.

questions.stem: Two squares have side lengths √5 + √2 and √5 − √2 respectively. What is the product of their areas?
questions.explanation: The product of the side lengths is (√5 + √2)(√5 − √2) = 5 − 2 = 3. The product of the areas is the square of that product, 9.

questions.stem:
The third term of a geometric sequence is 18 and the sixth term is −486.

What is the sum of the first four terms?

The fifth term of an arithmetic sequence is 17 and the sum of the first ten terms is 185.

What is the twentieth term?
questions.explanation: a + 4d = 17 and 5(2a + 9d) = 185, so 2a + 9d = 37. Subtracting 2(a + 4d) = 34 gives d = 3, a = 5. u₂₀ = 5 + 19 × 3 = 62.

questions.stem: What is the term independent of x in the expansion of (x + 2/x)⁶?
questions.explanation: The general term is ⁶Cᵣ x^(6−r)(2/x)ʳ, independent of x when r = 3: 20 × 8 = 160.

questions.stem:
A(1, 2) and B(7, 10) are the ends of a diameter of a circle.

What is the equation of the circle?
questions.explanation: Centre = midpoint (4, 6). AB = √(36 + 64) = 10, so the radius is 5 and r² = 25.

questions.stem:
A sector of a circle of radius 6 cm has an arc length of 4π cm.

What is the area of the sector?
questions.explanation: s = rθ gives θ = 4π/6 = 2π/3. Area = ½r²θ = ½ × 36 × 2π/3 = 12π. (Or area = ½rs = ½ × 6 × 4π.)

questions.stem: What is the exact value of sin(π/3) cos(π/6) + tan(π/4)?
questions.explanation: sin(π/3) = cos(π/6) = √3/2, so their product is 3/4. tan(π/4) = 1. Total 7/4.

questions.stem: What are the amplitude and period of the graph y = 3sin(2x)?
questions.explanation: The factor 3 stretches vertically (amplitude 3). sin(2x) completes a cycle twice as fast, so the period is 2π/2 = π.
27^(x − 1) = 3^(3x − 3). Equate powers: 2x + 1 = 3x − 3, so x = 4.

questions.stem: Solve log₃(x + 1) − log₃(x − 1) = 1.
questions.explanation: log₃[(x + 1)/(x − 1)] = 1, so (x + 1)/(x − 1) = 3 and x + 1 = 3x − 3, giving x = 2 (which keeps both logs defined).

questions.stem: Given y = (x² + 1)²/x, what is dy/dx when x = 1?
questions.explanation: Expand: y = x³ + 2x + x⁻¹. dy/dx = 3x² + 2 − x⁻². At x = 1: 3 + 2 − 1 = 4.

questions.stem:
An open box is made from a 12 cm by 12 cm square sheet by cutting a square of side x cm from each corner and folding up the sides.

What is the maximum possible volume of the box?
questions.explanation: V = x(12 − 2x)² = 4x³ − 48x² + 144x. dV/dx = 12x² − 96x + 144 = 12(x − 2)(x − 6) = 0. x = 6 gives zero volume, so x = 2: V = 2 × 8² = 128.

questions.stem: For which values of x is f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 9x decreasing?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x − 9 = 3(x + 1)(x − 3), which is negative between its roots: −1 < x < 3.

questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₀³ (x + 1)(x − 3) dx.
questions.explanation: Expand: x² − 2x − 3. [x³/3 − x² − 3x]₀³ = 9 − 9 − 9 = −9. Negative because the curve is below the x-axis for 0 < x < 3.

questions.stem: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve y = x(4 − x) and the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Roots at 0 and 4. ∫₀⁴ (4x − x²) dx = [2x² − x³/3]₀⁴ = 32 − 64/3 = 32/3.

questions.stem:
The point (2, −3) lies on the curve y = f(x).

Which point must lie on the curve y = 1 − f(−x)?
questions.explanation: f(−x) uses x = −2 to reach f(2) = −3. Then y = 1 − (−3) = 4. The point is (−2, 4).

questions.stem: For n > 1, let a = n^(1/2) and b = n^(−1/3). Which expression equals n^(1/6) for every such n?
questions.explanation: Multiplying powers of n adds the exponents. In ab the exponent is 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6.

questions.stem:
The line y = 2x + k is a tangent to the curve y = x² − 4x + 3.

What is k?
questions.explanation: x² − 4x + 3 = 2x + k gives x² − 6x + (3 − k) = 0. Tangent means equal roots: 36 − 4(3 − k) = 0, so 24 + 4k = 0 and k = −6.

questions.stem: How many solutions does tan x = √3 sin x have in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π?
questions.explanation: sin x (1/cos x − √3) = 0. sin x = 0 gives 0, π, 2π. cos x = 1/√3 gives two solutions (one in each of the first and fourth quadrants). Total 5. Do not divide by sin x.

questions.stem:
A geometric series has common ratio (x − 1)/2.

For which values of x does it have a sum to infinity?
At which point do the graphs y = 2ˣ and y = 8 − 2ˣ intersect?
questions.explanation: 2ˣ = 8 − 2ˣ gives 2 × 2ˣ = 8, so 2ˣ = 4, x = 2 and y = 4.

questions.stem:
The curve y = x³ + ax² + bx has a stationary point at (1, −4).

What is the value of b?
questions.explanation: y(1) = 1 + a + b = −4 and y′(1) = 3 + 2a + b = 0. Subtracting: 2 + a = 4, so a = 2 and b = −7.

questions.stem: How many distinct real roots does x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: Let u = x²: u² − 5u + 4 = 0, so u = 1 or 4. x = ±1, ±2: four roots.

questions.stem: What is the shortest distance from the point (8, 7) to the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 9?
questions.explanation: Centre (2, −1), radius 3. Distance from (8, 7) to the centre = √(36 + 64) = 10. Shortest distance to the circle = 10 − 3 = 7.

questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₀⁸ x^(1/3) dx.
